newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity names managers for some key funds.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity names managers for some key funds.

text.p: Fidelity Investments, the nation's largest mutual fund company, said Monday it named new managers in key funds under its taxable fixed-income division.

It said it named as portfolio managers Kevin Grant, for its broad market investment grade mutual funds; Charles Morrison, for the investment grade fixed-income sub-portfolio of its Asset Manager funds; Curtis Hollingworth for the government market mutual funds; and Andrew Dudley for the short-term investment grade mutual funds.
Grant, Morrison and Hollingsworth will manage funds previously run by Michael Gray and Bob Ives, who are leaving to pursue new opportunities, it said. Dudley succeeds Morrison, it added.
The company also said it has appointed Thomas Silvia co-manager, with Grant, of Fidelity Mortgage Securities Fund. He will join Grant in that fund, which Grant has run since 1993.
